keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Kwararafa row). The infobox gives "c. 13th/14th/15th century - c. 1840" and the page puts the state "along the Benue River Valley in central Nigeria", south of the Hausa states and southwest of Bornu, with capitals Santolo (founded "circa 1000"), Pindiga, Tagara (1380), Bepi/Kwararafa, Uka and Wukari. No outline is given. The start year is a bridge across the three centuries.

ledger.note: About 1300: Kwararafa exists. The infobox dates the start "c. 13th/14th/15th century"; "the first capital of the state, [Santolo], was founded circa 1000". In 1260 the Katsina account has Katsina fight "a war against Kwararafa". 1300 is a bridging year.
1380: the centre shifts to Tagara. "In 1380, possibly immediately after the conquest [of Santolo by Kano under Yaji, 1349-1385], the centre of Kwararafa shifted to Tagara."

wars.name: Kwararafa and the Hausa states

zones.text: Kwararafa 'centered along the Benue River Valley in what is today central Nigeria' (the page gives no outline; Taraba, with Wukari, and Benue stand for it)

wars.outcome: Kano under Yaji (1349-1385) captured Santolo; Kwararafa then paid tribute to Kano under Kanajegi (1390-1410) and to Zazzau for most of the 15th century; it suffered a devastating defeat by Bornu in the late 15th century; attacked Kano in the late 16th and early 17th centuries (Kano's ruler exiled 1653; refuge at Daura again 1671), and in 1680 assaulted Katsina and Zazzau and invaded Bornu, sacking its capital, until Ali III expelled them.
wars.note: Dates are the page's; only 1260, 1380, 1653, 1671 and 1680 are years, the rest are reigns or centuries.

certainty.note: The page gives the Benue valley and a list of capitals with almost no dates; the state is a confederacy and the outline is a guess.

notes:
Kwararafa (Jukun confederacy), additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Page: Kwararafa (one page; the name is also Kororofa).

The page gives no founding date; the infobox start "c. 13th/14th/15th century" is bridged to 1300. The end is c. 1840 (infobox), against "collapsed by the early 19th century" (body) and a Jukun dynasty at Wukari by 1820. The 1680 raid (Katsina, Zazzau, Bornu) and the tribute to Zazzau (15th century), Kano (1390-1410) and Bornu (end of the 18th century) belong in the suzerains' ledgers: none of those dossiers records them, and the kano and katsina dossiers of this batch should be checked for Kwararafa. The Benue valley prefectures are stand-ins.
Gazetteer: Santolo, Pindiga, Tagara, Bepi, Uka, Wukari (gazetteer).
